improvement_reason: The original code had overlapping x-axis labels and misalignment of bars, making the chart difficult to read. The improvement includes increasing the figure size for better visibility, adjusting bar positioning to ensure proper alignment, rotating x-axis labels to prevent overlap, and adding grid lines to enhance readability. Additionally, `plt.tight_layout()` is used to optimize spacing and prevent label clipping.
original_query: Create a bar chart to compare the Preqin Median Net IRR and LN PME Using S&P 500 TR for each Vintage year.
optimized_code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

df = pd.read_csv('table_name.csv')
bar_width = 0.35
index = np.arange(len(df['Vintage']))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
bar1 = ax.bar(index - bar_width / 2, df['Preqin Median Net IRR'], bar_width, label='Preqin Median Net IRR')
bar2 = ax.bar(index + bar_width / 2, df['LN PME Using S&P 500 TR'], bar_width, label='LN PME Using S&P 500 TR')

plt.xlabel('Vintage Year')
plt.ylabel('Values')
plt.title('Comparison of Preqin Median Net IRR and LN PME Using S&P 500 TR by Vintage Year')
plt.xticks(index, df['Vintage'], rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
